links.outcome: Triage under-triage and over-triage errors, safety of advice in LLM vignette triage
links.effect: Non-prompted safety of advice 89.06% mean, over-triage 53.15%; prompted safety 94.53%, over-triage 65.62%. Under-triage rarer but present, e.g., emergent pneumonia triaged to 1-week.
links.quote: Less common, but clinically more concerning, were under-triage errors, in which emergent cases such as pneumonia were occasionally categorized into “1-week.”

links.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of LLMs on clinical vignettes, including consistently missed diagnoses
links.effect: Mean diagnostic accuracy 89.84% non-prompted, 91.67% prompted; all models missed cases 1, 18 (HUS misdiagnosed as gastroenteritis/E. coli), and 42.
links.quote: For diagnostic predictions, all evaluated large language models (LLMs) consistently produced incorrect diagnoses for cases numbered 1, 18, and 42.

unlisted_practices: Answer-revealing in-context example prompting (47 solved cases) to improve LLM diagnosis and triage accuracy
Role prompting as a senior physician

links.effect: Mean diagnostic accuracy 89.84% non-prompted and 91.67% prompted; mean triage accuracy 76.82% and 86.20%.
links.quote: Structured prompting improved performance across models: mean diagnostic accuracy increased from 89.84% to 91.67%, and mean triage accuracy increased from 76.82% to 86.20%.

links.effect: Safety of advice rose from 89.06% to 94.53%, while over-triage rose from 53.15% to 65.62%.
links.quote: Safety of advice nearly reached a ceiling (94.53%) while over-triage rose substantially (from 53.15% to 65.62%).

links.effect: Best LLM diagnosis reached 93.75% versus physician benchmark 96%; triage remained lower than physicians, who correctly classified 91%.
links.quote: However, triage accuracy for these models remained lower than that of physicians, with systematic tendencies toward over-triage.

unlisted_practices: Structured answer-revealing prompting with exemplar cases improved LLM diagnosis and triage accuracy but increased over-triage.

links.effect: Over-triage occurred in 53.15% of errors without prompts and 65.62% with prompts; safety of advice was 89.06% and 94.53%; emergent cases such as pneumonia were occasionally under-triaged to 1-week.
links.quote: Error analyses showed predominant over-triage, with rarer but clinically important under-triage.
